assumptions: The cited international failure and replacement observations are treated as directional context rather than Polish cohort-specific incidence.
The family installer can introduce consenting pilot accounts but provides no owned customer relationship, exclusive distribution, inventory right, or confidential data.
All site-specific diagnosis, grid compliance, and installation decisions would be made by appropriately qualified parties.
No material inventory is purchased before paid cohort demand is demonstrated, despite the broader concept allowing up to 100,000 PLN of capital.
evidence_needed_for_higher_score: A model-and-serial-level regional fleet census; repeated documented stockouts and costly lead times for a specific unsupported cohort; paid reservations and renewals; field-validated compatibility; binding provenance and replenishment terms; signed liability allocations; and fully loaded realized cohort economics after failures, returns, misdiagnosis, and write-downs.

factors.name: Core insight
factors.rationale: Aging PV electronics, discontinued components, and the cost of inverter downtime create a plausible need for faster replacement access. The insight is weakened because the evidence establishes general failure and downtime, not recurring scarcity for any named Polish cohort, and established repowering routes can solve the same problem without preserving legacy hardware.

factors.name: Customer pain and willingness to pay
factors.rationale: Downtime, diagnostics, parts obligations, and modernization are genuine budgeted events, and OEM warranty-extension prices offer a useful willingness-to-pay reference. However, there is no evidence that owners prefer or will prepay for this third-party annual reservation rather than warranty, O&M stocking, repair, or planned repowering.

factors.name: Business model and economics
factors.rationale: Prepaid reservations could improve cash conversion, but the model combines low-frequency, model-specific demand with inventory acquisition, testing, storage, financing, warranty, misdiagnosis, obsolescence, and disposal risk. The proposed pricing and margin are hypotheses, and no cohort-level fully loaded economics show that reservations cover acquisition cost, write-downs, support, and channel share while producing attractive owner earnings.

factors.name: Market and beachhead
factors.rationale: Poland has a large installed PV base, and a narrow cohort of unsupported, operationally critical commercial systems could form a coherent beachhead. Yet the relevant denominator after filtering by model, age, warranty, support state, site criticality, lead time, and compatibility is unknown, so the economically reachable segment may be much smaller and more fragmented than the broad installed-base figure suggests.

factors.name: Competitive position and domination potential
factors.rationale: Owning tested stock for a genuinely scarce cohort could create local response-time leadership. Presently, no reserve, exclusive supply, protected allocation, validated interchangeability map, or customer contract is owned, while OEMs, distributors, refurbishers, and O&M firms can reproduce the reserve or steer customers to current-model replacement.

factors.name: Expansion potential
factors.rationale: A successful cohort could extend to additional inverter families, regions, loaners, adapters, and related availability services, with observed failures improving selection. Expansion remains capital intensive and operationally fragmented unless the business first proves that data can identify profitable cohorts and that replenishment and renewals recur.

factors.name: Defensibility and durability
factors.rationale: Inventory ownership and accumulated fleet, failure, repair, and interchangeability data could compound, but neither the supply position nor the data advantage exists yet. Ordinary O&M stocking clauses, OEM pools, distributor access, and repowering offers are durable substitutes, and a profitable named cohort would be visible and copyable.

factors.name: Strength of advantage
factors.rationale: Immediate access to a tested compatible unit could materially reduce downtime where OEM support has ended and repowering is slow or costly. The advantage is conditional: eligible OEM replacements may ship within roughly 48 hours, unauthorized provenance can reduce value, and site-specific electrical, firmware, certification, and transformer constraints may prevent a pooled unit from being usable.

factors.name: Timing and momentum
factors.rationale: A growing installed base and the roughly 10-15 year technical life cited for inverters support an emerging aging-fleet need. At the same time, current-product repowering and tightening certification requirements can accelerate replacement away from legacy equipment, so age alone does not create a favorable stocking window.

factors.name: Distribution
factors.rationale: The family renewable installer offers a lawful route to a bounded consenting pilot, and installer/O&M portfolios are logical aggregation channels. No customer ownership, signed channel access, acquisition cost, conversion rate, or partner commitment is evidenced, and channel partners may prefer to own the customer and internalize the stock themselves.

factors.name: Execution and risks
factors.rationale: The founder's analytical skills fit cohort selection, but safe execution requires authentic sourcing, electrical testing, qualified diagnosis and installation, provenance, conformity analysis, insurance, storage, logistics, warranty handling, and disposal. These physical and regulated dependencies are difficult to manage part-time, and the full 100,000 PLN ordinary capital allowance could be trapped in slow-moving stock.

highest_value_structural_change: Make inventory acquisition conditional on a named cohort having prepaid multi-site commitments that cover purchase, testing, storage, insurance, expected write-downs, and support, together with qualified-engineer validation of the exact interchangeability envelope and protected-provenance supply terms.
main_structural_strength: The offer ties a measurable downtime loss to a concrete availability promise and can, in principle, use prepaid cohort reservations to avoid wholly speculative inventory purchases.
primary_score_limiter: The economic mechanism requires a narrow cohort to be scarce enough to justify advance payment yet large and compatible enough to pool, while established OEM, O&M, repair, and repowering alternatives constrain both price and demand; none of those cohort-level conditions is established.
strongest_disconfirming_evidence: OEMs publicly describe rapid eligible replacement and cross-brand repowering routes, while ordinary O&M practice can include planned replacement inverters; this directly challenges the claimed gap and makes a third-party reserve readily substitutable for supported equipment.
